A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ThinkMorph study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. Matching relocated material and image-based case studies supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark comparisons, test-time scaling results, and mode-switching analyses in Sections 3–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds computational-cost measurements, a larger-data text-only control, and textual-output analyses.

M1.justification: The Bagel-based model, interleaved generation procedure, modality delimiters, training objectives, and data-construction methods remain unchanged. New Appendix B.2 explains the existing reasoning modes rather than introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four training tasks and evaluation coverage, including VSP, VisPuzzle, ChartQA, VStar, BLINK-J, MMVP, SAT, BLINK, and CV-Bench. The additional analyses concern retained tasks; the fourfold-data control changes sample quantity without identifying a new domain or task.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same reasoning-mode comparators and external models, including GPT-4o, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, InternVL3.5, Qwen2.5-VL, Janus-Pro, Chameleon, and Bagel. The added fourfold-data control uses the existing text-only method under a different training budget.

E3.justification: V3 adds a text-only control trained with four times more samples, token-cost measurements, and entropy/vocabulary metrics computed on correct predictions (Appendices B.3–B.4). These extend the evaluation settings; the retained benchmark protocols, main training configurations, inference temperatures, and sampling budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices B.3–B.4 substantially expand supplementary analysis by examining computational cost, testing whether additional text-only training closes the performance gap, and comparing textual entropy and vocabulary. Section 4 also adds token-consumption evidence to the existing mode-switching comparison. The original scaling analyses and Appendix C case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version provides new independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Sampling budgets remain unchanged; the added entropy and vocabulary measurements characterize outputs rather than uncertainty in reported performance.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 retain their accuracies, but v3 adds substantial quantitative evidence about cost and textual diversity. New results include BLINK-J costs of 1,073 versus 354 tokens for interleaved versus text reasoning at N=1, fourfold-data text-only accuracies of 55.50% on VStar and 47.17% on VSP, and entropy/vocabulary comparisons in Table 7. Section 4 adds the 156-versus-89-token comparison, while Table 5 supplies absolute scores for the scaling analysis already plotted in Figure 7.

T1.justification: The formal interleaved-sequence description and training objectives are unchanged. Appendix B.2 provides explanatory sequence templates, and the new empirical metrics introduce no formal definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about complementary modalities, generalization, emergent manipulations, autonomous switching, and test-time scaling. The new analyses support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: V3 acknowledges approximately threefold token cost at equal sampling budgets, argues that extra text-only training does not explain the advantage, and interprets lexical diversity as enrichment of textual representations. These extend the existing mechanism account. However, Appendix B.3's new lower-cost interpretation conflicts with its own 4,269-versus-2,879-token comparison.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.2 makes the mode-specific token sequences explicit and clarifies their shared visual-thought data. Existing hardware, learning rates, training steps, loss weights, inference settings, and resource links are retained; v1's hyperparameter Table 5 becomes v3's Table 8 without numerical changes.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive positioning against prior multimodal reasoning and unified-model research are unchanged. Citation formatting and grammatical corrections do not alter that positioning.

P1.justification: V3 adds explanatory appendix subsections and an expanded roadmap, standardizes 'visual-only' terminology, corrects grammar and the Frozen Lake text-thought prompt heading, and updates affiliations and the conference header. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact; the expanded roadmap contains an unresolved 'Section ??' reference.

P2.justification: V3 adds Tables 5–7, relocates Figure 6 and Table 3, and incorporates the existing hyperparameter table into the training-details page. Figure 2 revises the maze illustration and corrects visual-search answer choices. These are localized display changes; the overall design and Appendix C case-study images remain intact.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves transparency by quantifying previously unreported computational costs, adding a larger-data text-only control, and clarifying reasoning-mode formats. These help readers assess the retained performance claims. The gains are limited by underdescribed compute matching and textual-diversity measurements, and especially Appendix B.3's incorrect assertion that 4,269 tokens are fewer than 2,879. The useful additional evidence supports a limited overall improvement, not a substantial strengthening of the conclusions.
